question.:question/problem:
Given that

$$
S=\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 4 & -8 \\ -1 & -8 & 0 \\ 8 & -2 & -1\end{bmatrix}
$$

which of the following elementary row operations makes $a_{11}=0$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Of the given options, we consider the row operation

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-{R}_{2}.
$$

At the requested entry, this gives

$$
a_{11}=-1+(-1)\cdot (-1)=0.
$$

Applying the above row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}S &=\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 4 & -8 \\ -1 & -8 & 0 \\ 8 & -2 & -1\end{bmatrix}\qquad {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-{R}_{2} \\ &\sim \begin{bmatrix}0 & 12 & -8 \\ -1 & -8 & 0 \\ 8 & -2 & -1\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-{R}_{2}.
$$

question.:question/problem:

Of the given options, we consider the row operation

$$

$$

The entry in row $3$, column $1$ is $0$. Switching rows $1$ and $3$ therefore makes $a_{11}=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}S &=\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 4 & -8 \\ 11 & -8 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -1\end{bmatrix}\qquad {R}_{3}↔{R}_{1} \\ &\sim \begin{bmatrix}0 & -2 & -1 \\ 11 & -8 & 0 \\ -1 & 4 & -8\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{3}↔{R}_{1}.
$$
